reasons.specificity: The analysis maps Castoriadis's specific arguments—'rational mastery,' Cambridge School critique, Kaleckian distribution theory, the Trente Glorieuses, the neoliberal counter-offensive—onto distinct CAP rows rather than using generic market-failure templates, and the actors (Thatcher/Reagan, Nike workers in Indonesia, Kalecki's 1943 prediction) are drawn from the actual text rather than generic categories.
reasons.anchoring: Most quoted passages are verbatim and correctly placed—'guided solely by the short-term view of their profits,' 'Nothing prevents them from doing so. But also, nothing guarantees that they will do so,' 'kept capitalism from drowning in its own production'—but a few interpretive leaps occur: CAP6 labels oligopolistic market power a 'coordination failure against consumers,' whereas the source treats it as a feature of market structure, not a cooperation problem; and the 'assurance game' framing of CAP7 is an analytical imposition not supported by any game-theoretic language in the text.
reasons.non_obviousness: The analysis surfaces non-obvious distinctions: free-riding on 'free gifts of history' (social knowledge as a non-excludable public good); the asymmetric power of interest-rate policy (central banks can choke expansion but not reliably sustain it, citing Keynes's note); the internal bureaucratic-clan dynamics that displace rational maximization; and the counter-evidence that Castoriadis himself concedes capitalism may persist even while causing severe harm.
reasons.coherence: The actors/shared-outcome/incentive/barrier rows are internally consistent and the responses table correctly separates existing cooperation (ES1–ES6), proposed arrangements (PS1–PS5), and unresolved constraints; the severity ratings and feasibility assessments are consistent with the textual evidence cited, and the findings ledger aligns with the structured tables.
reasons.usefulness: The requested artifact is delivered fully: actors/shared-outcome/incentive/barrier rows for seven CAPs, a responses table distinguishing existing from proposed solutions with effectiveness and feasibility ratings, free-rider and coordination-failure sub-analyses, and open questions pointing to genuine gaps left by the source—all of which orient a reader working through this dense essay.
reasons.hallucination_risk: No major facts are invented, but several analytical framings are imported without textual warrant: labeling CAP7 an 'assurance game,' classifying CAP4 as 'other' while calling it a prisoner's dilemma in the prose framing, and asserting that capital controls (ES4) were previously 'effective' when the text does not directly evaluate their past effectiveness—it only notes their current removal. The 'chicken game' label for CAP5 is a plausible interpretation but is not textually grounded.

decisive_errors.claim: CAP7 is characterized as an 'assurance game' in which individuals retreat because they lack confidence others will participate.
decisive_errors.counter_passage: The text attributes political passivity to 'the bankruptcy of the traditional left-wing parties, the trade unions' enormous loss of influence, the monstrosity of the regimes of actually existing socialism, the apathy and privatization of whole populations, and their growing irritation with the hypertrophic growth and absurdity of state bureaucracies'—a multi-causal account of organizational collapse, not a strategic assurance-game payoff structure.

score.one_line: A thorough, source-grounded cooperation-problem reading with well-chosen quotes and a complete actors/solutions table, slightly undermined by a few game-theoretic framings (assurance game, chicken) imported without textual warrant.
